afghanistan.text: Afghanistan is a landlocked mountainous country located on the Iranian Plateau, at the crossroads of Central Asia and South Asia. The country is the 40th largest in the world in size. Kabul is the capital and largest city of Afghanistan, located in the middle of Kabul Province.
afghanistan.title: Geography of Afghanistan

afghanistan.text: The history of present-day Afghanistan in the pre-modern times is largely shared with the neighbouring regions in Central, South and West Asia.
afghanistan.title: History of Afghanistan

afghanistan.text: The culture of Afghanistan has persisted for centuries and encompasses the cultural diversity of the nation. Its location at the crossroads of Central, South and West Asia historically made it a hub of diversity, dubbed by one historian as the "roundabout of the ancient world".
afghanistan.title: Culture of Afghanistan

afghanistan.text: Afghanistan has a developing economy that is considered low income and among the world's least developed. With a population of around 43 million people, the nation generates $19.66 billion in nominal gross domestic product and $101 billion by purchasing power parity GDP, as of 2026.
afghanistan.title: Economy of Afghanistan

aland.text: The Åland archipelago consists of several thousands of islands, skerries and desolate rocks. About 60-80 islands are inhabited. In the east, the archipelago is connected to Archipelago Sea off the city of Turku.
aland.title: Geography of Åland

aland.text: The history of the Åland Islands spans more than six thousand years, from early human settlement to modern autonomy within Finland. Archaeological finds show that the islands have been inhabited continuously since the Neolithic period.
aland.title: History of Åland

aland.text: Åland is an autonomous and demilitarised region of Finland. Receiving its autonomy in 1920, it is the smallest region of Finland by both area and population, constituting 0.51% of Finland's land area and 0.54% of its population.
aland.title: Economy of Åland

albania.text: Albania is a country in southeastern Europe that lies along the Adriatic and Ionian Seas, with a coastline spanning approximately 476 km. Situated on the Balkan Peninsula, it is one of the most mountainous countries in Europe.
albania.title: Geography of Albania

albania.text: During classical antiquity, Albania was home to several Illyrian tribes such as the Albanoi, Ardiaei, Bylliones, Dassaretii, Enchele, Labeatae, Taulantii, Parthini, Penestae, Amantes, and many others, but also Bryges and Epirote tribes, as well as several Greek colonies established on the Illyrian coast in cooperation with the local Illyrians, notably Epidamnos-Dyrrhachium and Apollonia.
albania.title: History of Albania

albania.text: Albanian culture or the culture of Albanians is a term that embodies the artistic, culinary, literary, musical, political and social elements that are representative of ethnic Albanians, which implies not just Albanians of the country of Albania but also Albanians of Kosovo, North Macedonia and Montenegro, where ethnic Albanians are a native population.
albania.title: Culture of Albania

albania.text: The economy of Albania is a developing mixed economy. Since the early 2000s, the economy transitioned from a centralized to a mixed, free-market economic system. Its largest sectors are services, agriculture, and industry.
albania.title: Economy of Albania

algeria.text: Algeria comprises 2,381,740 square kilometres of land, more than 80% of which is desert, in North Africa, between Morocco and Tunisia. It is the largest country in Africa since the 2011 breakup of Sudan, and the creation of South Sudan.
algeria.title: Geography of Algeria

algeria.text: Algeria's history has been shaped by its position between the Mediterranean, the Maghreb, and the Sahara.
algeria.title: History of Algeria

algeria.text: The culture of Algeria encompasses literature, music, religion, cuisine, and other facets of life in Algeria.
algeria.title: Culture of Algeria

algeria.text: Algeria has a mixed market economy. Since independence in 1962, Algeria has launched major economic projects to build up a dense industrial base. However, despite these major achievements, the Algerian economy has gone through various stages of turbulence.
algeria.title: Economy of Algeria

american-samoa.text: American Samoa is a self-governing, unincorporated and unorganized territory of the United States located in the south Pacific Ocean, within the Polynesia subregion of Oceania.
american-samoa.title: Geography of American Samoa

american-samoa.text: The islands of Samoa were originally inhabited by humans as early as 1000 BC. After being invaded by European colonists in the 18th century, by the 20th and 21st century, the islands were incorporated into Samoa and American Samoa.
american-samoa.title: History of American Samoa

picture.credit: U.S. Government Accountability Office from Washi

american-samoa.text: The economy of American Samoa is a traditional Polynesian economy in which more than 90% of the land is communally owned.
american-samoa.title: Economy of American Samoa

andorra.text: Andorra is a small, landlocked country in southwestern Europe, located in the eastern Pyrenees mountain range and bordered by Spain and France. With an area of 468 km², it is the sixth smallest country in Europe and also the largest of the European microstates.
andorra.title: Geography of Andorra

andorra.text: Andorra, officially the Principality of Andorra, also called the Principality of the Valleys of Andorra, is a sovereign landlocked microstate in southwestern Europe, located in the eastern Pyrenees mountain range and is bordered by Spain and France.
andorra.title: History of Andorra

andorra.text: Andorra is essentially Catalan-speaking. The country has contributed significantly to Catalan heritage.
andorra.title: Culture of Andorra

andorra.text: The economy of Andorra is a developed and free market economy driven by finance, retail, and tourism. The country's gross domestic product was US$6.00 billion in 2024. Attractive for shoppers from France and Spain as a free port, Andorra also has developed active summer and winter tourist resorts.
andorra.title: Economy of Andorra

angola.text: Angola is located on the western Atlantic Coast of Southern Africa between Namibia and the Republic of the Congo. It also is bordered by the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zambia to the east.
angola.title: Geography of Angola

angola.text: Angola was first settled by San hunter-gatherer societies before the northern domains came under the rule of Bantu states such as Kongo and Ndongo. In the 15th century, Portuguese colonists began trading, and a settlement was established at Luanda during the 16th century.
angola.title: History of Angola

angola.text: The culture of Angola is influenced by the Portuguese. Portugal occupied the coastal enclave Luanda, and later also Benguela, since the 16th/17th centuries, and expanded into the territory of what is now Angola in the 19th/20th centuries, ruling it until 1975.
angola.title: Culture of Angola

angola.text: Angola has a semi-planned economy, in which central planning directs the economy with the participation of private enterprises.
angola.title: Economy of Angola

anguilla.text: Anguilla is an island in the Leeward Islands. It has numerous bays, including Barnes, Little, Rendezvous, Shoal, and Road Bays.
anguilla.title: Geography of Anguilla

anguilla.text: The economy of Anguilla depends heavily on luxury tourism, offshore banking, lobster fishing, and remittances from emigrants.
anguilla.title: Economy of Anguilla

antigua-and-barbuda.text: Antigua and Barbuda lie in the eastern arc of the Leeward Islands of the Lesser Antilles, separating the Atlantic Ocean from the Caribbean Sea. Antigua is 650 km southeast of Puerto Rico; Barbuda lies 48 km due north of Antigua, and the uninhabited island of Redonda is 56 km southwest of Antigua.
antigua-and-barbuda.title: Geography of Antigua and Barbuda

antigua-and-barbuda.text: The history of Antigua and Barbuda covers the period from the arrival of the Archaic peoples thousands of years ago to the present day. Prior to European colonization, the lands encompassing present-day Antigua and Barbuda were inhabited by three successive Amerindian societies.
antigua-and-barbuda.title: History of Antigua and Barbuda

picture.credit: Just a Brazilian man from Brazil

antigua-and-barbuda.text: The traditions of West Africa and the United Kingdom have the biggest impact on the culture of Antigua and Barbuda. As a crucial component of its culture, Antigua and Barbuda also has its own creole language.
antigua-and-barbuda.title: Culture of Antigua and Barbuda

antigua-and-barbuda.text: The economy of Antigua and Barbuda is service-based, with tourism and government services representing the key sources of employment and income. Tourism accounts directly or indirectly for more than half of GDP and is also the principal earner of foreign exchange in Antigua and Barbuda.
antigua-and-barbuda.title: Economy of Antigua and Barbuda

argentina.text: The geography of Argentina is heavily diverse, consisting of the Andes Mountains, pampas, and various rivers and lakes.
argentina.title: Geography of Argentina

argentina.text: The history of Argentina can be divided into four main parts: the pre-Columbian time or early history, the colonial period, the period of nation-building, and the history of modern Argentina.
argentina.title: History of Argentina

argentina.text: The culture of Argentina is as varied as the country's geography and is composed of a mix of ethnic groups.
argentina.title: Culture of Argentina

argentina.text: The economy of Argentina is the second-largest in South America, behind Brazil. The United Nations' Human Development Index ranks Argentina "very high," reflecting a literate population, export-oriented agriculture, and diversified industry.
argentina.title: Economy of Argentina

armenia.text: Armenia is a landlocked country in the South Caucasus region of the Caucasus. The country is geographically located in West Asia, within the Armenian plateau.
armenia.title: Geography of Armenia

armenia.text: The history of Armenia covers the topics related to the history of the Republic of Armenia, as well as the Armenian people, the Armenian language, and the regions of Eurasia historically and geographically considered Armenian.
armenia.title: History of Armenia

armenia.text: The culture of Armenia encompasses many elements that are based on the geography, literature, architecture, dance, and music of the Armenian people. Armenia is a majority Christian country in the Caucasus.
armenia.title: Culture of Armenia

armenia.text: Armenia has an emerging free-market economy. It is the 112th-largest economy in the world in nominal terms, with an estimated gross domestic product of almost $34 billion. In terms of purchasing power parity, Armenia's GDP surpasses $83 billion and is ranked 109th in the world.
armenia.title: Economy of Armenia

picture.credit: NASA World Wind, Screenshot by Carport

aruba.text: The geography of Aruba, located at the juncture of the South American and Caribbean tectonic plates, has been shaped by a complex interplay of geological processes.
aruba.title: Geography of Aruba

aruba.text: The economy of Aruba is classified as a high income economy by the World Bank, with tourism currently providing the largest percentage of the country's income. Because of tourism's rapid growth on the island in the last 80 years, related industries like construction have also flourished in Aruba.
aruba.title: Economy of Aruba

picture.credit: Reto Stöckl / NASA Goddard Space Flight Center

australia.text: Australia, officially the Commonwealth of Australia, is a sovereign country comprising the mainland of the Australian continent, the island state of Tasmania, and thousands of minor islands. It occupies a total area of 7,688,287 km2, making it the sixth-largest country in the world.
australia.title: Geography of Australia

australia.text: The Commonwealth of Australia was proclaimed on 1 January 1901 as a federation of six self-governing former British colonies.
australia.title: History of Australia

australia.text: Australian culture is of primarily Western origins, and is derived from its British, Indigenous and migrant components. Aboriginal Australians arrived as early as 60,000 years ago, and evidence of Aboriginal art in Australia dates back at least 30,000 years.
australia.title: Culture of Australia

picture.credit: U.S. Navy photo by Petty Officer 2nd Class David

australia.text: Australia has a highly developed mixed economy. As of 2026, Australia was the 12th-largest national economy by nominal GDP, the 22nd-largest by PPP-adjusted GDP, and was the 21st-largest goods exporter and 24th-largest goods importer.
australia.title: Economy of Australia

austria.text: Austria is a predominantly mountainous country in Central Europe, approximately between Germany, Italy and Hungary. It has a total area of 83,871 square kilometres.
austria.title: Geography of Austria

austria.text: The history of Austria covers the history of Austria and its predecessor states. In the late Iron Age Austria was occupied by people of the Hallstatt Celtic culture, they first organized as a Celtic kingdom referred to by the Romans as Noricum, dating from c. 800 to 400 BC.
austria.title: History of Austria

austria.text: Austrian culture is characterised by historical and modern influences, including a history of interaction primarily between Celtic, Roman, Slavic and Germanic peoples.
austria.title: Culture of Austria

austria.text: Austria has a highly developed social market economy, with the country being one of the 28 richest in the world in terms of GDP per capita. Until the 1980s, many of its largest industry firms were nationalised.
austria.title: Economy of Austria

picture.credit: Jeff Schmaltz, MODIS Rapid Response Team, NASA/G

azerbaijan.text: Azerbaijan is a country in the Caucasus region, situated at the juncture of Eastern Europe and West Asia.
azerbaijan.title: Geography of Azerbaijan

azerbaijan.text: In this article, the history of Azerbaijan is understood as the history of the region now forming the Republic of Azerbaijan. Topographically, the land is contained by the southern slopes of the Caucasus Mountains in the north, the Caspian Sea in the east, and the Armenian Highlands in the west.
azerbaijan.title: History of Azerbaijan

azerbaijan.text: The culture of Azerbaijan combines a diverse and heterogeneous set of elements which developed under the influence of Iranic, Turkic and Caucasian cultures. Azerbaijani culture includes its cuisine, literature, folk art, architecture and music.
azerbaijan.title: Culture of Azerbaijan

picture.credit: Press Service of the President of the Republic o

azerbaijan.text: The economy of Azerbaijan is a developing upper-middle-income transition economy that is highly dependent on oil and gas exports, in particular since the completion of the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan Pipeline.
azerbaijan.title: Economy of Azerbaijan

bahrain.text: The Kingdom of Bahrain consists of Bahrain Island and 33 of the 37 Bahrain Islands, lying in the Persian Gulf's Gulf of Bahrain off the north shore of West Asia's Arabian Peninsula. Bahrain's capital city is Manama.
bahrain.title: Geography of Bahrain

bahrain.text: The culture of Bahrain is part of the historical region of Eastern Arabia. Thus, Bahrain's culture is similar to that of its Arab neighbours in the Persian Gulf region. Bahrain is known for its cosmopolitanism, Bahraini citizens are very ethnically diverse.
bahrain.title: Culture of Bahrain

bahrain.text: The economy of the Kingdom of Bahrain has significantly diversified in recent years to be less dependent on oil and gas, although they remain an important part of the economy. As of 2024, the extraction of oil and natural gas is the third largest sector in the economy.
bahrain.title: Economy of Bahrain

bangladesh.text: Bangladesh is a densely populated, low-lying, mainly riverine country located in South Asia with a coastline of 580 km on the northern littoral of the Bay of Bengal. The delta plain of the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna Rivers and their tributaries occupy 79 percent of the country.
bangladesh.title: Geography of Bangladesh

bangladesh.text: The history of Bangladesh dates back over four millennia to the Chalcolithic period. The region's early history was characterized by a succession of Hindu and Buddhist kingdoms and empires that fought for control over the Bengal region.
bangladesh.title: History of Bangladesh

bangladesh.text: The culture of Bangladesh has evolved over the centuries and encompasses the cultural diversity of several social groups of the country.
bangladesh.title: Culture of Bangladesh

bangladesh.text: The economy of Bangladesh is a developing, market-oriented economy. In the 2025–26 fiscal year its nominal GDP was estimated at US$501 billion, making it the second-largest economy in South Asia. As of 2026, it ranked 36th in nominal terms and 26th by purchasing power parity.
bangladesh.title: Economy of Bangladesh

barbados.text: Barbados is a continental island in the Atlantic Ocean east of the Caribbean and is located at 13°10' north of the equator, and 59°32' west of the Prime Meridian.
barbados.title: Geography of Barbados

barbados.text: Barbados is an island country in the southeastern Caribbean Sea, situated about 100 miles east of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. Roughly triangular in shape, the island measures some 21 miles from northwest to southeast and about 14 miles from east to west at its widest point.
barbados.title: History of Barbados

picture.credit: The original uploader was ROxBo at English Wikip

barbados.text: The culture of Barbados is a blend of West African and British cultures present in Barbados. English is the official language of the nation, reflecting centuries of British influence, but the Bajan dialect in which it is spoken is an iconic part of the Barbadian culture.
barbados.title: Culture of Barbados

barbados.text: Since the island country's independence in 1966, the economy of Barbados has been transformed from a low-income economy dependent upon sugar production into a high-income economy based on service-driven industries and the offshore sector.
barbados.title: Economy of Barbados

belarus.text: Belarus is a landlocked country that occupies an area of 207,600 square kilometers. It lacks natural borders, and the average elevation of Belarus is 162 meters above sea level.
belarus.title: Geography of Belarus

belarus.text: The lands of Belarus during the Middle Ages became part of Kievan Rus' and were split between different regional principalities, including Polotsk, Turov, Vitebsk, and others.
belarus.title: History of Belarus

belarus.text: Belarusian culture is the product of a millennium of development under the impact of a number of diverse factors.
belarus.title: Culture of Belarus

belarus.text: Belarus has an upper-middle income mixed economy. As a post-Soviet transition economy, the nation rejected most privatisation efforts in favour of retaining centralised political and economic controls by the state.
belarus.title: Economy of Belarus

belgium.text: Belgium is a federal state located in Western Europe and is divided into three regions: the Flemish Region, the Walloon Region, and the Brussels Capital Region. Belgium borders the North Sea and shares borders with the countries of France, the Netherlands, Germany and Luxembourg.
belgium.title: Geography of Belgium

picture.credit: Claes Janszoon Visscher II / Joannes van Doetecu

belgium.text: For most of its history, what is today Belgium was either a part of a larger territory, such as the medieval Carolingian Empire, or was divided into a number of smaller states.
belgium.title: History of Belgium

belgium.text: The culture of Belgium involves both the aspects shared by all Belgians regardless of the language they speak and the differences between the main cultural communities: the Dutch-speaking Belgians and the French-speaking Belgians.
belgium.title: Culture of Belgium

belgium.text: Belgium has a highly developed high-income mixed economy. The Belgian economy has capitalised on the country's central geographic location, and has a well-developed transport network, and diversified industrial and commercial base.
belgium.title: Economy of Belgium

picture.credit: Jacques Descloitres, MODIS Land Rapid Response T

belize.text: Belize is a small Central American nation, located at 17°15' north of the equator and 88°45' west of the Prime Meridian on the Yucatán Peninsula. It borders the Caribbean Sea to the east, with 386 km of coastline.
belize.title: Geography of Belize

belize.text: The history of Belize dates back thousands of years. The Maya civilization spread into the area of Belize between 1500 BC to 1200 BC and flourished until about 1000 AD.
belize.title: History of Belize

belize.text: The culture of Belize is a mix of influences and people from Kriol, Maya, East Indian, Garinagu, Mestizo, Mennonites who are of German descent, with many other cultures from Chinese to Lebanese. It is a unique blend that emerged through the country's long and occasionally violent history.
belize.title: Culture of Belize

picture.credit: Willamor Media from Cary, NC, USA

belize.text: Belize has a developing economy. It is a small, essentially private enterprise economy that is based primarily on agriculture, tourism, and services. The cultivation of newly discovered oil in the town of Spanish Lookout has presented new prospects and problems for this developing nation.
belize.title: Economy of Belize

benin.text: Benin, a narrow, key-shaped, north–south strip of land in West Africa, lies between the Equator and the Tropic of Cancer. Its latitude ranges from 6°30′ N to 12°30′ N and its longitude from 1° E to 3°40′ E.
benin.title: Geography of Benin

benin.text: Early evidence of human settlement in the area of modern Benin can be found in the Atakora mountain chain of north-western Benin. Systematic surveys and excavations have identified caves, rock shelters and open-air sites with lithic industries spanning the Early, Middle and Later Stone Age.
benin.title: History of Benin

benin.text: Benin, officially the Republic of Benin, formerly known as Dahomey, is a country in West Africa. It is bordered by Togo to the west, Nigeria to the east, Burkina Faso to the northwest, and Niger to the northeast.
benin.title: Culture of Benin

benin.text: Benin has a developing economy dependent on subsistence agriculture and cotton. Cotton accounts for 40% of its GDP and roughly 80% of official export receipts. There is also production of textiles, palm products, and cocoa beans.
benin.title: Economy of Benin

bermuda.text: Bermuda is an overseas territory of the United Kingdom in the North Atlantic Ocean.
bermuda.title: Geography of Bermuda

bermuda.text: Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory comprising a number of islands, with an area of 54 km2, located in the North Atlantic Ocean, which in 2016 had a population of 65,331.
bermuda.title: Economy of Bermuda

bhutan.text: Bhutan is a sovereign country at the crossroads of East Asia and South Asia, located towards the eastern extreme of the Himalayas mountain range. It is fairly evenly sandwiched between the sovereign territory of two nations: first, the People's Republic of China on the north and northwest.
bhutan.title: Geography of Bhutan

bhutan.text: Bhutan's early history is steeped in mythology and remains obscure. Some of the structures provide evidence that the region has been settled as early as 2000 BC. In the 12th century, the Drukpa Kagyupa school was established and remains the dominant form of Buddhism in Bhutan today.
bhutan.title: History of Bhutan

bhutan.text: Cradled in the folds of the Himalayas, Bhutan has relied on its geographical isolation to protect itself from outside cultural influences.
bhutan.title: Culture of Bhutan

bhutan.text: The economy of Bhutan is based on agriculture and forestry, which provide the main livelihood for more than 60% of the population. Agriculture consists largely of subsistence farming and animal husbandry.
bhutan.title: Economy of Bhutan

bolivia.text: The geography of Bolivia includes the Eastern Andes Mountain Range which bisects Bolivia roughly from north to south.
bolivia.title: Geography of Bolivia

bolivia.text: The history of Bolivia involves thousands of years of human habitation. Lake Titicaca had been an important center of culture and development for thousands of years.
bolivia.title: History of Bolivia

bolivia.text: Bolivia is a country in South America, bordered by Brazil to the north and east, Paraguay and Argentina to the south, Chile to the west, and Peru to the west. The cultural development of what is now Bolivia is divided into three distinct periods: pre-Columbian, colonial, and republican.
bolivia.title: Culture of Bolivia

bolivia.text: The economy of Bolivia is the 89th-largest in the world in nominal terms and the 90th-largest in purchasing power parity. Bolivia is classified by the World Bank to be a lower middle income country. With a Human Development Index of 0.703, it is ranked 114th.
bolivia.title: Economy of Bolivia

bosnia-and-herzegovina.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina is located in Southeastern Europe. Situated in the western Balkans, it has a 932 km border with Croatia to the north and southwest, a 357 km border with Serbia to the east, and a 249 km border with Montenegro to the southeast.
bosnia-and-herzegovina.title: Geography of Bosnia and Herzegovina

bosnia-and-herzegovina.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina is a country in Southeast Europe on the Balkan Peninsula. It has had permanent settlement since the Neolithic Age. By the early historical period it was inhabited by Illyrians and Celts.
bosnia-and-herzegovina.title: History of Bosnia and Herzegovina

bosnia-and-herzegovina.text: The culture of Bosnia and Herzegovina encompasses the country's ancient heritage, architecture, science, literature, visual arts, music, cinema, sports and cuisine.
bosnia-and-herzegovina.title: Culture of Bosnia and Herzegovina

bosnia-and-herzegovina.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina has a developing transitional economy. Since its independence movement during the 1990s, the country has sought deeper economic integration within Europe. Their main trading partner is the European Union and neighboring countries in Southeast Europe.
bosnia-and-herzegovina.title: Economy of Bosnia and Herzegovina

botswana.text: Botswana is a landlocked country located in Southern Africa, north of South Africa. Botswana occupies an area of 581,730 square kilometres.
botswana.title: Geography of Botswana

botswana.text: The history of Botswana encompasses the region's ancient and tribal history, its colonisation as the Bechuanaland Protectorate, and the present-day Republic of Botswana. The first modern humans to inhabit Botswana were the San people, and agriculture first developed approximately 2,300 years ago.
botswana.title: History of Botswana

botswana.text: Botswana has a developing economy considered upper-middle income. Growth in private sector employment averaged about 10% per annum during the first 30 years of the country's independence.
botswana.title: Economy of Botswana

brazil.text: The country of Brazil occupies roughly half of South America, bordering the Atlantic Ocean. Brazil covers a total area of 8,514,215 km2 which includes 8,456,510 km2 of land and 55,455 km2 of water. The highest point in Brazil is Pico da Neblina at 2,994 m.
brazil.title: Geography of Brazil

brazil.text: Before the arrival of the Europeans, the lands that now constitute Brazil were inhabited and settled by diverse tribes for thousands of years.
brazil.title: History of Brazil

brazil.text: The culture of Brazil has been shaped by the amalgamation of diverse indigenous cultures, and the cultural fusion that took place among Indigenous communities, Portuguese colonists, and Africans, primarily during the Brazilian colonial period.
brazil.title: Culture of Brazil

brazil.text: Brazil has a diversified mixed economy. It is the largest in Latin America, the Southern Hemisphere and the second in Americas, in nominal terms. As of 2026, it is an upper-middle income and developing economy with the second largest GDP in the Americas in nominal and purchasing power parity terms.
brazil.title: Economy of Brazil

british-indian-ocean-territory.text: The geography of the Chagos Archipelago concerns a group of coral atolls, reefs and submerged banks in the central Indian Ocean, at the southern end of the Chagos–Laccadive Ridge, which continues northwards through the Maldives and Lakshadweep.
british-indian-ocean-territory.title: Geography of the Chagos Archipelago

british-virgin-islands.text: The British Virgin Islands are one of three political divisions of the Virgin Islands archipelago located in the Lesser Antilles, between the Caribbean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean. The BVI are the easternmost part of the island chain.
british-virgin-islands.title: Geography of the British Virgin Islands

british-virgin-islands.text: The economy of the British Virgin Islands is one of the most prosperous in the Caribbean. Although tiny in absolute terms, because of the very small population of the British Virgin Islands, in 2010 the Territory had the 19th highest GDP per capita in the world according to the CIA World factbook.
british-virgin-islands.title: Economy of the British Virgin Islands

brunei.text: Brunei is a country in Southeast Asia, bordering the South China Sea and East Malaysia. Its geographical coordinates are 4°30′N 114°40′E. The country is small with a total size of 5,765 km2. It is larger in size than Trinidad and Tobago.
brunei.title: Geography of Brunei

brunei.text: The history of Brunei concerns the settlements and societies located on the north coast of the island of Borneo, which has been under the influence of Indianised kingdoms and empires for much of its history.
brunei.title: History of Brunei

brunei.text: The culture of Brunei is strongly influenced by Malay culture and Islam.
brunei.title: Culture of Brunei

brunei.text: The economy of Brunei, a small and wealthy country, is a mixture of foreign and domestic entrepreneurship, government regulation and welfare measures, and village traditions.
brunei.title: Economy of Brunei

bulgaria.text: Bulgaria is a country situated in Southeast Europe that occupies the eastern quarter of the Balkan peninsula, being the largest country within its geographic boundaries.
bulgaria.title: Geography of Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: The history of Bulgaria can be traced from the first settlements on the lands of modern Bulgaria to its formation as a nation-state, and includes the history of the Bulgarian people and their origins.
bulgaria.title: History of Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: Bulgarian culture has deep roots in the traditions of the indigenous Thracian heritage and the Slavic peoples who settled the Balkans in the early Middle Ages.
bulgaria.title: Culture of Bulgaria

bulgaria.text: The economy of Bulgaria functions on the principles of the free market, having a large private sector and a smaller public one. Bulgaria has an advanced, high-income economy according to the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
bulgaria.title: Economy of Bulgaria

burkina-faso.text: Burkina Faso is a landlocked Sahel country that shares borders with six nations. It lies between the Sahara desert and the Gulf of Guinea, south of the loop of the Niger River, mostly between latitudes 9° and 15°N, and longitudes 6°W and 3°E.
burkina-faso.title: Geography of Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: The history of Burkina Faso includes the history of various kingdoms within the country, such as the Mossi kingdoms, as well as the later French colonisation of the territory and its independence as the Republic of Upper Volta in 1960.
burkina-faso.title: History of Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: The culture of Burkina Faso in West Africa is also called the Burkinabé culture. Two key elements of culture in Burkina Faso are its indigenous masks and dancing. The masks used in this region of the western Sahel are made for rites of sacrifice to gods and animal spirits in the villages.
burkina-faso.title: Culture of Burkina Faso

burkina-faso.text: Burkina Faso has a developing, low-income economy. It is based primarily on subsistence farming and livestock raising. Burkina Faso has a low average income level, with GDP per capita estimated at $3,000 and $1,100 in the mid-2020s.
burkina-faso.title: Economy of Burkina Faso

burundi.text: Burundi is located in East Africa, to the east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, at the coordinates 3°30′S 30°0′E.
burundi.title: Geography of Burundi

burundi.text: Burundi originated in the 16th century as a small kingdom in the African Great Lakes region. After European contact, it was united with the Kingdom of Rwanda, becoming the colony of Ruanda-Urundi - first colonised by Germany and then by Belgium.
burundi.title: History of Burundi

burundi.text: The culture of Burundi is based on local tradition and common influence with its neighbors.
burundi.title: Culture of Burundi

burundi.text: Burundi has a developing economy. It generates $9.21 billion by gross domestic product as of 2026, being heavily dependent on agriculture, which accounts for 32.9% of gross domestic product as of 2008.
burundi.title: Economy of Burundi

cambodia.text: Cambodia is a country in mainland Southeast Asia. It borders Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, the Gulf of Thailand and covers a total area of approximately 181,035 km2. The country is situated in its entirety inside the tropical Indomalayan realm and the Indochina Time zone.
cambodia.title: Geography of Cambodia

cambodia.text: The history of Cambodia, a country in mainland Southeast Asia, begins with the earliest evidence of habitation around 5000 BCE.
cambodia.title: History of Cambodia

cambodia.text: Throughout Cambodia's long history, religion has been a major source of cultural inspiration. Over nearly two millennia, Cambodians have developed a unique Cambodian culture and belief system from the syncreticism of indigenous animistic beliefs and the Indian religions of Buddhism and Hinduism.
cambodia.title: Culture of Cambodia

cambodia.text: Cambodia's economy currently follows an open market system and has seen rapid economic progress in the last decade. Cambodia's two largest industries are textiles and tourism, while agricultural activities remain the main source of income for many Cambodians living in rural areas.
cambodia.title: Economy of Cambodia

cameroon.text: At 475,440 km2, Cameroon is the world's 53rd largest country. It is slightly larger than the nation of Sweden and the US state of California. It is comparable in size to Papua New Guinea. Cameroon's landmass is 472,710 km2, with 2,730 km2 of water.
cameroon.title: Geography of Cameroon

cameroon.text: At the crossroads of West Africa and Central Africa, the territory of what is now Cameroon has seen human habitation since some time in the Middle Paleolithic, likely no later than 130,000 years ago.
cameroon.title: History of Cameroon

cameroon.text: Cameroon has a rich and diverse culture made up of a mix of about 250 indigenous populations and just as many languages and customs.
cameroon.title: Culture of Cameroon

cameroon.text: Cameroon has a developing economy considered lower-middle income. It was one of the most prosperous in Africa for a quarter of a century after independence.
cameroon.title: Economy of Cameroon

canada.text: Canada has a vast geography that occupies much of the continent of North America, sharing a land border with the contiguous United States to the south and the U.S. state of Alaska to the northwest.
canada.title: Geography of Canada

canada.text: The history of Canada covers the period from the arrival of the Paleo-Indians to North America thousands of years ago to the present day.
canada.title: History of Canada

canada.text: The culture of Canada embodies the artistic, culinary, literary, humour, musical, political and social elements that are representative of Canadians.
canada.title: Culture of Canada

canada.text: Canada has an advanced and diversified mixed economy. The nation relies upon its abundant natural resources and well-developed international trade networks. As of 2026, it is the eleventh-largest in the world in nominal terms.
canada.title: Economy of Canada

cape-verde.text: Cabo Verde, officially known as Republic of Cabo Verde, is a group of arid Atlantic islands which are home to distinct communities of plants, birds, and reptiles.
cape-verde.title: Geography of Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: The recorded human history of Cabo Verde begins with the Portuguese discovery of the island in 1458. Possible early references to Cape Verde date back at least 2,000 years.
cape-verde.title: History of Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: The culture of Cape Verde is rich, with a range of customs and practices common in the islands.
cape-verde.title: Culture of Cape Verde

cape-verde.text: Cape Verde has a developing economy that is service-oriented with a focus on commerce, trade, transport and public services. It is a small archipelagic nation that lacks resources and has experienced severe droughts.
cape-verde.title: Economy of Cape Verde

cayman-islands.text: The Cayman Islands are a British dependency and island country. It is a three-island archipelago in the Caribbean Sea, consisting of Grand Cayman, Cayman Brac, and Little Cayman.
cayman-islands.title: Geography of the Cayman Islands

picture.credit: Roger W from Sarasota, Florida, U.S.A.

cayman-islands.text: The economy of the Cayman Islands, a British overseas territory located in the western Caribbean Sea, is mainly fueled by the tourism sector and by the financial services sector, together representing 50–60 percent of the country's gross domestic product.
cayman-islands.title: Economy of the Cayman Islands

central-african-republic.text: The Central African Republic is a landlocked nation within the interior of the African continent. It is bordered by Cameroon, Chad, Sudan, South Sudan, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of the Congo.
central-african-republic.title: Geography of the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: The history of the Central African Republic is roughly composed of four distinct periods. The earliest period of settlement began around 10,000 years ago when nomadic people first began to settle, farm and fish in the region. The next period began around 10,000 years prior.
central-african-republic.title: History of the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: The Central African Republic is a landlocked country in Central Africa. It is bordered by Chad to the north, Sudan to the northeast, South Sudan to the east, the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the south, the Republic of the Congo to the southwest, and Cameroon to the west.
central-african-republic.title: Culture of the Central African Republic

central-african-republic.text: The Central African Republic has a developing economy. It generates $2.321 billion by gross domestic product as of 2019, with an estimated annual per capita income of just $529 as measured nominally in 2024. Sparsely populated and landlocked, the Central African Republic is overwhelmingly agrarian.
central-african-republic.title: Economy of the Central African Republic

chad.text: Chad is one of the world's landlocked countries and is located in Central Africa, measuring 1,284,000 square kilometers, approximately 2.4 times the size of metropolitan France and slightly more than three times the size of California.
chad.title: Geography of Chad

chad.text: Chad, officially the Republic of Chad, is a landlocked country in Central Africa. It borders Libya to the north, Sudan to the east, the Central African Republic to the south, Cameroon and Nigeria to the southwest, and Niger to the west.
chad.title: History of Chad

chad.text: Chad, officially the Republic of Chad, is a landlocked country in Central Africa. It is bordered by Libya to the north, Sudan to the east, the Central African Republic to the south, Cameroon to the southwest, Nigeria to the southwest, and Niger to the west.
chad.title: Culture of Chad

chad.text: Chad has a developing economy. It suffers from the landlocked country's geographic remoteness, drought, lack of infrastructure, and political turmoil. About 80% of the population depends on subsistence agriculture, including livestock herding.
chad.title: Economy of Chad

chile.text: The geography of Chile is extremely diverse, as the country extends from a latitude of 17° South to Cape Horn at 56°, and from the Pacific Ocean in the west to the Andes in the east.
chile.title: Geography of Chile

chile.text: The territory of Chile has been populated since at least 3000 BC. By the 16th century, Spanish invaders began to raid the region of present-day Chile, and the territory was a colony from 1540 to 1818, when it gained independence from Spain.
chile.title: History of Chile

chile.text: The culture of Chile reflects the population and the geographic isolation of the country in relation to the rest of South America.
chile.title: Culture of Chile

chile.text: Chile has a developing market economy. It is classified as a high-income economy by the World Bank, and is recognized as one of the most prosperous countries in South America.
chile.title: Economy of Chile

colombia.text: The Republic of Colombia is situated largely in the north-west of South America, with some territories falling within the boundaries of Central America.
colombia.title: Geography of Colombia

colombia.text: The history of Colombia includes its settlement by indigenous peoples and the establishment of agrarian societies, notably the Muisca Confederation, Quimbaya Civilization, and Tairona Chiefdoms.
colombia.title: History of Colombia

colombia.text: Many aspects of Colombian culture can be traced back to the early culture of Spain of the 16th century and its collision with Colombia's native civilizations. The Spanish brought Catholicism, the feudal encomienda system, and a caste system that favored European descendants.
colombia.title: Culture of Colombia

colombia.text: Colombia has the fourth largest economy in Latin America as measured by gross domestic product and the third-largest economy in South America.
colombia.title: Economy of Colombia

comoros.text: The Comoros archipelago consists of four main islands aligned along a northwest–southeast axis at the north end of the Mozambique Channel, between Mozambique and the island of Madagascar.
comoros.title: Geography of the Comoros

comoros.text: The history of the Comoros extends back to about 800–1000 AD when the archipelago was first inhabited. The Comoros have been inhabited by various groups and sultanates throughout this time. France colonised the islands in the 19th century, and they became independent in 1975.
comoros.title: History of the Comoros

comoros.text: The Comoros, officially the Union of the Comoros, is an archipelagic country made up of three islands in Southeast Africa, located at the northern end of the Mozambique Channel in the Indian Ocean. Its capital and largest city is Moroni.
comoros.title: Culture of the Comoros

comoros.text: Comoros has a developing economy based on subsistence agriculture and fishing. It has inadequate transportation links, a young and rapidly increasing population, and few natural resources.
comoros.title: Economy of the Comoros

cook-islands.text: The Cook Islands is located in Oceania, in the South Pacific Ocean, about halfway between Hawaii and New Zealand. The country can be divided into two groups: the Southern Cook Islands and the Northern Cook Islands. Rarotonga in the southern group is the main island.
cook-islands.title: Geography of the Cook Islands

picture.credit: Print made by Rev. John Williams (1796-1839), Pr

cook-islands.text: The Cook Islands are named after Captain James Cook, who visited the islands in 1773 and 1777, although Spanish navigator Alvaro de Mendaña was the first European to reach the islands in 1595.
cook-islands.title: History of the Cook Islands

picture.credit: NZ Ministry of Foreign Affairs / New Zealand Hig

cook-islands.text: The economy of the Cook Islands is based mainly on tourism, with minor exports of tropical and citrus fruit. Manufacturing activities in the Cook Islands are limited to fruit-processing, clothing and handicrafts.
cook-islands.title: Economy of the Cook Islands

costa-rica.text: Costa Rica is located on the Central American Isthmus, surrounding the point 10° north of the equator and 84° west of the prime meridian. It has 212 km of Caribbean Sea coastline and 1,016 on the North Pacific Ocean.
costa-rica.title: Geography of Costa Rica

costa-rica.text: The first indigenous peoples of Costa Rica were hunters and gatherers, and when the Spanish conquerors arrived, Costa Rica was divided in two distinct cultural areas due to its geographical location in the Intermediate Area, between Mesoamerican and the Andean cultures, with influences of both cultures.
costa-rica.title: History of Costa Rica

costa-rica.text: Costa Rican culture has been heavily influenced by Spanish culture ever since the Spanish colonization of the Americas including the territory which today forms Costa Rica.
costa-rica.title: Culture of Costa Rica

costa-rica.text: The economy of Costa Rica has been very stable for some years now, with continuing growth in the GDP and moderate inflation, though with a high unemployment rate: 11.49% in 2019. Costa Rica's economy emerged from recession in 1997 and has shown strong aggregate growth since then.
costa-rica.title: Economy of Costa Rica

croatia.text: The geography of Croatia is defined by its location at the crossroads of Central Europe and Southeast Europe, and the wider region of Southern Europe. Croatia's territory covers 56,594 km2, making it the 127th largest country in the world.
croatia.title: Geography of Croatia

croatia.text: At the height of the Roman Empire, the area of modern Croatia comprised two Roman provinces, Pannonia and Dalmatia. After the collapse of the Western Roman Empire in the 5th century, the area was subjugated by the Ostrogoths for 50 years, before being incorporated into the Byzantine Empire.
croatia.title: History of Croatia

croatia.text: The culture of Croatia has historically been influenced by Central European, Mediterranean, and Balkan cultures. Croatia's unique culture and identity can be traced back to the historical llyricum.
croatia.title: Culture of Croatia

croatia.text: Croatia has a highly developed mixed economy. It is one of the largest economies in Southeast Europe by nominal gross domestic product. It maintains a similarly high regional GDP per capita.
croatia.title: Economy of Croatia

cuba.text: Cuba is an island nation in the Caribbean Sea. It comprises an archipelago of islands centred upon the geographic coordinates 21°3N, 80°00W. Cuba is the principal island, surrounded by four main archipelagos: the Colorados, the Sabana-Camagüey, the Jardines de la Reina and the Canarreos.
cuba.title: Geography of Cuba

cuba.text: The island of Cuba was inhabited by various Indigenous cultures prior to the arrival of the explorer Christopher Columbus in 1492. After his arrival, Spain conquered Cuba and appointed Spanish governors to rule in Havana.
cuba.title: History of Cuba

cuba.text: The culture of Cuba is a complex mixture of different, often contradicting, factors and influences. The Cuban people and their customs are based on European, African and Amerindian influences.
cuba.title: Culture of Cuba

cuba.text: Cuba has a developing command economy dominated by state-run enterprises. The Communist Party of Cuba maintains high levels of public sector control and exerts significant influence over the Cuban economy.
cuba.title: Economy of Cuba

curacao.text: Curaçao, as well as the rest of the ABC islands and Trinidad and Tobago, lies on the continental shelf of South America. It is a thin island with a generally hilly topography; the highest point is Christoffelberg 372 m in the northwest.
curacao.title: Geography of Curaçao

curacao.text: The economy of Curaçao is a high income economy, as defined by the World Bank. The island has a well-developed infrastructure with strong tourism and financial services sectors.
curacao.title: Economy of Curaçao

cyprus.text: Cyprus is an island in the Eastern Basin of the Mediterranean Sea. It is the third-largest island in the Mediterranean, after the Italian islands of Sicily and Sardinia, and the 80th-largest island in the world by area. It is located south of the Anatolian Peninsula, and belongs to the Cyprus Arc.
cyprus.title: Geography of Cyprus

cyprus.text: Human habitation of Cyprus dates back to the Paleolithic era. Cyprus's geographic position has caused the island to be influenced by differing Eastern Mediterranean civilizations over millennia.
cyprus.title: History of Cyprus

cyprus.text: Cyprus, officially the Republic of Cyprus, is an island country in the eastern Mediterranean Sea, located off the coast of the Levant mainland in West Asia.
cyprus.title: Culture of Cyprus

cyprus.text: The economy of Cyprus is a high-income economy as classified by the World Bank, and was included by the International Monetary Fund in its list of advanced economies in 2001.
cyprus.title: Economy of Cyprus

czech-republic.text: The Czech Republic is a landlocked country in Central Europe. It is bordered by Germany to the west, Austria to the south, Slovakia to the east and Poland to the north. It consists mostly of low hills and plateaus surrounded along the borders by low mountains.
czech-republic.title: Geography of the Czech Republic

czech-republic.text: The history of the Czech lands – an area roughly corresponding to the present-day Czech Republic – starts approximately 800,000 years BCE. A simple chopper from that age was discovered at the Red Hill archaeological site in Brno.
czech-republic.title: History of the Czech lands

czech-republic.text: Czech culture has been shaped by the nation's geographical position in Central Europe, the Slavic origins of the Czech people, neighbouring influences, and political and social developments, including periods of war and peace.
czech-republic.title: Culture of the Czech Republic

czech-republic.text: The Czech Republic has a developed export-oriented social market economy. It is based in services, manufacturing, and innovation that maintains a high-income welfare state and the European social model.
czech-republic.title: Economy of the Czech Republic

democratic-republic-of-the-congo.text: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is the largest country of sub-Saharan Africa, occupying 2,344,858 square kilometres. The country lies on the equator. Most of the country lies within the vast hollow of the Congo River Basin.
democratic-republic-of-the-congo.title: Geography of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

democratic-republic-of-the-congo.text: The earliest known human settlements in what is now the Democratic Republic of the Congo date back to the Middle Stone Age, approximately 90,000 years ago.
democratic-republic-of-the-congo.title: History of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

democratic-republic-of-the-congo.text: The culture of the Democratic Republic of the Congo is extremely varied, reflecting the great diversity and different customs which exist in the country.
democratic-republic-of-the-congo.title: Culture of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

democratic-republic-of-the-congo.text: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has a developing transition economy.
democratic-republic-of-the-congo.title: Economy of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

denmark.text: Denmark is a Nordic country located in Northern Europe. It consists of the Jutland Peninsula and several islands in the Baltic Sea, referred to as the Danish Archipelago.
denmark.title: Geography of Denmark

denmark.text: The history of Denmark as a unified kingdom began in the 8th century, but prehistoric cultures populated the area for about 12,000 years, since the end of the last ice age. Historic descriptions of the area and people from around 500 AD include writings by Jordanes and Procopius.
denmark.title: History of Denmark

denmark.text: The culture of Denmark has a rich artistic and scientific heritage.
denmark.title: Culture of Denmark

denmark.text: Denmark has a modern high-income and highly developed social democratic economy, dominated by the service sector with 80% of all jobs; about 11% of employees work in manufacturing and 2% in agriculture.
denmark.title: Economy of Denmark

djibouti.text: Djibouti is a country in the Horn of Africa. It is bordered by Eritrea in the north, Ethiopia in the west and south, and Somalia in the southeast. To the east is its coastline on the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. Rainfall is sparse, and most of the territory has a semi-arid to arid environment.
djibouti.title: Geography of Djibouti

djibouti.text: Djibouti is a country in the Horn of Africa bordered by Somalia to the east, Eritrea to west and the Red Sea to the north, Ethiopia to the west and south, and the Gulf of Aden to the east. In antiquity, the territory was part of the Land of Punt. Djibouti gained its independence on June 27, 1977.
djibouti.title: History of Djibouti

djibouti.text: The culture of the Republic of Djibouti is diverse due to the nation's Red Sea location at a crossroads of trade and commerce.
djibouti.title: Culture of Djibouti

djibouti.text: Djibouti has a developing economy. Its economic potential is derived in large part from its strategic location on the Red Sea. Djibouti is mostly barren, with little development in the agricultural and industrial sectors.
djibouti.title: Economy of Djibouti

dominica.text: Dominica is an island in the Caribbean Sea, located about halfway between the French islands of Guadeloupe and Martinique. Its coordinates are 15 25 N, 61 20 W.
dominica.title: Geography of Dominica

dominica.text: The first written records in the history of Dominica began in November 1493, when Christopher Columbus spotted the island. Prior to European contact, Dominica was inhabited by the Arawak.
dominica.title: History of Dominica

dominica.text: The culture of Dominica is formed by the inhabitants of the Commonwealth of Dominica. Dominica is home to a wide range of people. Although it was historically occupied by several native tribes, it was the Taíno and Kalinago tribes that remained by the time European settlers reached the island.
dominica.title: Culture of Dominica

dominica.text: The economy of Dominica is reliant upon agriculture, particularly bananas, with the financial services industry and citizenship by investment scheme becoming increasingly the island's largest source of income. Banana production employs, directly or indirectly, upwards of one-third of the work force.
dominica.title: Economy of Dominica

dominican-republic.text: The Dominican Republic is a country in the West Indies that occupies the eastern five-eighths of Hispaniola. It has an area of 48,670 km2, including offshore islands. The land border shared with Haiti, which occupies the western three-eighths of the island, is 376 km long.
dominican-republic.title: Geography of the Dominican Republic

dominican-republic.text: The recorded history of the Dominican Republic began in 1492 when Christopher Columbus, working for the Crown of Castile, arrived at a large island in the western Atlantic Ocean, later known as the Caribbean.
dominican-republic.title: History of the Dominican Republic

dominican-republic.text: The culture of the Dominican Republic is a diverse mixture of different influences from around the world. The Dominican people and their customs have origins consisting predominantly in a European cultural basis, with Indigenous and African influences.
dominican-republic.title: Culture of the Dominican Republic

dominican-republic.text: The economy of the Dominican Republic is the seventh largest in Latin America, and is the largest in the Caribbean and Central American region.
dominican-republic.title: Economy of the Dominican Republic

east-timor.text: Timor-Leste includes the mountainous eastern half of Timor, the Ocussi-Ambeno region on the northwest portion of the island of Timor, and the islands of Atauro and Jaco.
east-timor.title: Geography of Timor-Leste

east-timor.text: Timor-Leste, officially the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste, is an island country in Southeast Asia. The country comprises the eastern half of the island of Timor and the nearby islands of Atauro and Jaco. The first inhabitants are thought to be descendant of Australoid and Melanesian peoples.
east-timor.title: History of Timor-Leste

east-timor.text: The culture of Timor-Leste reflects numerous cultural influences, including Portuguese, Roman Catholic, and Malay, on the indigenous Austronesian cultures in Timor-Leste.
east-timor.title: Culture of Timor-Leste

east-timor.text: The economy of Timor-Leste is a lower-middle income economy as ranked by the World Bank. It is placed 142nd on the Human Development Index, indicating a medium level of human development. 20% of the population is unemployed, and 52.9% live on less than $1.25 a day.
east-timor.title: Economy of Timor-Leste

ecuador.text: Ecuador is a country in western South America, bordering the Pacific Ocean at the Equator, for which the country is named.
ecuador.title: Geography of Ecuador

ecuador.text: The History of Ecuador spans from the beginning of human habitation in the region from around 8,000 BC to present. During the Pre-Columbian era, various cultures influenced the people and land that today make up the contemporary Republic of Ecuador.
ecuador.title: History of Ecuador

ecuador.text: Ecuador is a multicultural and multiethnic nation, with the majority of its population is descended from a mixture of both European and Amerindian ancestry. The other 10% of Ecuador's population originate east of the Atlantic Ocean, predominantly from Spain, Italy, Lebanon, France and Germany.
ecuador.title: Culture of Ecuador

ecuador.text: The economy of Ecuador is the eighth largest in Latin America and the 69th largest in the world by total GDP. Ecuador's economy is based on the export of oil, bananas, shrimp, gold, other primary agricultural products and money transfers from Ecuadorian emigrants employed abroad.
ecuador.title: Economy of Ecuador

egypt.text: The geography of Egypt relates to two regions: North Africa and West Asia. Egypt has coastlines on the Mediterranean Sea, the River Nile, and the Red Sea. Egypt borders Libya to the west, Palestine and Israel to the east and Sudan to the south. Egypt has an area of 1,010,408 km2.
egypt.title: Geography of Egypt

egypt.text: Egypt, one of the world's oldest civilizations, was unified around 3150 BC by King Narmer. It later came under Persian, Greek, Roman, and Arab rule before being joined to the Ottoman Empire in 1517. Controlled by Britain in the late 19th century, it became a republic in 1953.
egypt.title: History of Egypt

egypt.text: The culture of Egypt has thousands of years of recorded history. A cradle of civilization, Ancient Egypt was among the earliest civilizations in the world. For millennia, Egypt developed strikingly unique, complex and stable cultures that influenced other cultures of Europe, Africa and Asia.
egypt.title: Culture of Egypt

egypt.text: Egypt has a developing mixed economy, combining private business with government regulation. It is the 2nd largest economy in Africa, and 41st in worldwide ranking as of 2026.
egypt.title: Economy of Egypt

el-salvador.text: El Salvador is a country in Central America. Situated at the meeting point of three tectonic plates, it has high seismological activity and is the location of numerous earthquakes and volcanic eruptions. The country has a tropical climate.
el-salvador.title: Geography of El Salvador

el-salvador.text: The history of El Salvador begins with several distinct groups of Mesoamerican people, especially the Pipil, the Lenca and the Maya. In the early 16th century, the Spanish Empire conquered the territory, incorporating it into the Viceroyalty of New Spain ruled from Mexico City.
el-salvador.title: History of El Salvador

el-salvador.text: The culture of El Salvador is a Central American culture nation influenced by the clash of ancient Mesoamerica and medieval Iberian Peninsula. Salvadoran culture is influenced by Native American culture as well as Latin American culture.
el-salvador.title: Culture of El Salvador

el-salvador.text: The economy of El Salvador is considered a developing, upper-middle-income economy that relies heavily on services, exports, foreign family remittances and its unique status as a dollarized country. It has experienced relatively low rates of GDP growth, in comparison to other developing countries.
el-salvador.title: Economy of El Salvador

equatorial-guinea.text: The Republic of Equatorial Guinea is located in west central Africa. Bioko Island lies about 40 kilometers from Cameroon. Annobón Island lies about 595 kilometres southwest of Bioko Island.
equatorial-guinea.title: Geography of Equatorial Guinea

equatorial-guinea.text: The History of Equatorial Guinea is marked by centuries of colonial domination by the Portuguese, British and Spanish colonial empires, and by the local kingdoms.
equatorial-guinea.title: History of Equatorial Guinea

picture.credit: Ben Sutherland from Crystal Palace, London, UK

equatorial-guinea.text: Lying on the culturally rich continent of Africa, Equatorial Guinea has proved to be entrenched in ancient rituals and songs.
equatorial-guinea.title: Culture of Equatorial Guinea

picture.credit: Ben Sutherland from Crystal Palace, London, UK

equatorial-guinea.text: Equatorial Guinea has a developing economy. It has normally traditionally been dependent on commodities such as cocoa and coffee, but is now heavily dependent on natural gasses due to the discovery and exploitation of significant oil reserves in the 1980s.
equatorial-guinea.title: Economy of Equatorial Guinea

eritrea.text: Eritrea is located in the Horn of Africa and is bordered on the northeast and east by the Red Sea, on the west and northwest by Sudan, on the south by Ethiopia, and on the southeast by Djibouti. The country has a high central plateau that varies from 1,800 to 3,000 meters above sea level.
eritrea.title: Geography of Eritrea

eritrea.text: Eritrea is an ancient name and is located in the Horn of Africa, associated in the past with its Greek form Erythraia, Ἐρυθραία, and its derived Latin form Erythræa. This name relates to that of the Red Sea, then called the Erythræan Sea, from the Greek for "red", ἐρυθρός, erythros.
eritrea.title: History of Eritrea

eritrea.text: The culture of Eritrea is the collective cultural heritage of the various populations native to Eritrea. Eritrea has nine recognized ethnic groups. Each group have their own unique traditions and customs but some traditions are shared and appreciated among different ethnic groups.
eritrea.title: Culture of Eritrea

eritrea.text: Eritrea has a developing economy. It relies on subsistence agriculture, rainfed farming, livestock, and fisheries; about 70% of the population lives in rural areas. The economy is tightly controlled, and all significant enterprises are state-owned.
eritrea.title: Economy of Eritrea

estonia.text: Between 57.3 and 59.5 latitude and 21.5 and 28.1 longitude, Estonia lies on the eastern coast of the Baltic Sea on the level northwestern part of the rising East European Platform.
estonia.title: Geography of Estonia

estonia.text: The history of Estonia forms a part of the history of Europe. Human settlement in what is now Estonia became possible 13,000–11,000 years ago, after the ice from the last glacial era had melted, and signs of the first permanent population in the region date from around 9000 BC.
estonia.title: History of Estonia

estonia.text: The culture of Estonia combines an indigenous heritage, represented by the country's Finnic national language Estonian, with Nordic and German cultural aspects. Over the centuries, the culture of modern Estonia has been significantly influenced by that of the Germanic-speaking world.
estonia.title: Culture of Estonia

estonia.text: Estonia has an advanced developed economy. It is a member of the European Union, the eurozone, and the OECD. The economy is heavily influenced by developments in the Finnish and Swedish economies.
estonia.title: Economy of Estonia

eswatini.text: Eswatini, is a country in Southern Africa lying between Mozambique and South Africa. The country is located at the geographic coordinates 26°30′S 31°30′E. Eswatini has an area of 17,363 square kilometres, of which 160 are water. The major regions of the country are Lowveld, Midveld and Highveld.
eswatini.title: Geography of Eswatini

eswatini.text: Artifacts indicating human activity dating back to the early Stone Age have been found in the Kingdom of Eswatini. The earliest known inhabitants of the region were Khoisan hunter-gatherers. Later, the population became predominantly Nguni during and after the great Bantu migrations.
eswatini.title: History of Eswatini

eswatini.text: Swazi culture is the way of life and customs of the Swazi people through various historical stages. The culture of Swazi people involves music, food, religion, architecture, and kinship, among many other things.
eswatini.title: Culture of Eswatini

eswatini.text: Eswatini has a diversified developing economy. Agriculture, forestry and mining account for about 13 percent of Eswatini's GDP, whereas manufacturing represent 37 percent of GDP. Services, with government services in the lead, constitute the other 50 percent of GDP.
eswatini.title: Economy of Eswatini

ethiopia.text: Ethiopia is located in the Horn of Africa. It is bordered by Eritrea to the north, Djibouti and Somalia to the east, Sudan and South Sudan to the west, and Kenya to the south.
ethiopia.title: Geography of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Ethiopia is one of the oldest countries in Africa; the emergence of Ethiopian civilization dates back thousands of years. Abyssinia or rather "Ze Etiyopia" was inhabited by Abyssinians, specifically the Amhara and Tigrayans and the Cushitic, Oromo and Agaw.
ethiopia.title: History of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: The culture of Ethiopia is diverse and generally structured along ethnolinguistic lines.
ethiopia.title: Culture of Ethiopia

ethiopia.text: Ethiopia has a mixed transition economy with a large public sector. The government of the Federal Republic of Ethiopia is in the process of privatizing many of the state-owned businesses and moving toward a market economy.
ethiopia.title: Economy of Ethiopia

falkland-islands.text: The culture of the Falkland Islands is essentially analogous to that of British culture, along with some influences of Hispanic America. The Falkland Islands have a large native-born population, mainly white and from England, but also from Saint Helena.
falkland-islands.title: Culture of the Falkland Islands

falkland-islands.text: The economy of the Falkland Islands, which first involved sealing, whaling and provisioning ships, became heavily dependent on sheep farming from the 1870s to 1980. It then diversified and now has income from tourism, commercial fishing, and servicing the fishing industry as well as agriculture.
falkland-islands.title: Economy of the Falkland Islands

faroe-islands.text: The Faroe Islands are an island group consisting of eighteen islands between the Norwegian Sea and the North Atlantic, about half-way between Iceland and Norway. Its coordinates are 62°N 7°W. It is 1,393 square kilometres in area, and includes small lakes and rivers, but no major ones.
faroe-islands.title: Geography of the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: The early details of the history of the Faroe Islands are unclear. It is possible that Brendan, an Irish monk, sailed past the islands during his North Atlantic voyage in the 6th century.
faroe-islands.title: History of the Faroe Islands

faroe-islands.text: The economy of the Faroe Islands was the 166th largest in the world in 2014, having a nominal gross domestic product of $2.613 billion per annum. GDP increased from DKK 8 billion in 1999, to 21 billion in 2019. The vast majority of Faroese exports, around 90%, consists of fishery products.
faroe-islands.title: Economy of the Faroe Islands

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: Geography of the Federated States of Micronesia, a country located in the western Pacific Ocean, and in the Micronesia cultural and ecological sub-region of Oceania. While its total land area is very small at 702 km2, it has the 14th largest exclusive economic zone at 2,996,419 km2.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Geography of the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: The Federated States of Micronesia are located on the Caroline Islands in the western Pacific Ocean.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: History of the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: The Federated States of Micronesia, or simply Micronesia, is an island country in Micronesia, a region of Oceania.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Culture of the Federated States of Micronesia

federated-states-of-micronesia.text: The economic activity of the Federated States of Micronesia consists primarily of subsistence agriculture and fishing. The islands have few mineral deposits worth exploiting, except for high-grade phosphate.
federated-states-of-micronesia.title: Economy of the Federated States of Micronesia

fiji.text: Fiji is an Oceanian archipelago of volcanic islands with two main islands in the South Pacific, lying about 1,770 km north of New Zealand and 4,450 kilometres southwest of Honolulu, Hawaii. Of the 332 islands and 522 smaller islets making up the archipelago, about 106 are permanently inhabited.
fiji.title: Geography of Fiji

picture.credit: Drawn by Joseph Drayton. Engraved by Rawdon, Wri

fiji.text: The majority of Fiji's islands were formed through volcanic activity starting around 150 million years ago. Today, some geothermic activity still occurs on the islands of Vanua Levu and Taveuni.
fiji.title: History of Fiji

fiji.text: The culture of modern-day Fiji is a blend of indigenous Fijian, Indian, European, Chinese cultures. Fiji had influence from various other cultures from the Pacific neighbors of Fiji; in particular the Tongan and Rotuman cultures.
fiji.title: Culture of Fiji

fiji.text: The economy of Fiji is one of the most developed among the Pacific islands. Nevertheless, Fiji is a developing country endowed with forest, mineral and fish resources. The country has a large agriculture sector heavily based on subsistence agriculture.
fiji.title: Economy of Fiji

finland.text: The geography of Finland is characterized by its northern position, its ubiquitous landscapes of intermingled boreal forests and lakes, and its low population density.
finland.title: Geography of Finland

finland.text: The history of Finland began around 9000 BC during the end of the last glacial period. Stone Age cultures were Kunda, Comb Ceramic, Corded Ware, Kiukainen, and Pöljä cultures. The Finnish Bronze Age started in approximately 1500 BC and the Iron Age started in 500 BC and lasted until 1300 AD.
finland.title: History of Finland

finland.text: The culture of Finland combines indigenous heritage, as represented for example by the country's national languages Finnish and Swedish, and the sauna, with common Nordic and European cultural aspects.
finland.title: Culture of Finland

finland.text: Finland has a highly developed mixed economy. It has a per capita output similar to that of western European economies such as France, Germany, and the United Kingdom.
finland.title: Economy of Finland

picture.credit: Jacques Descloitres, MODIS Rapid Response Team,

france.text: The geography of France consists of a terrain that is mostly flat plains or gently rolling hills in the north and the west and mountainous in the south and the east. Metropolitan France has a total size of 551,695 km2.
france.title: Geography of France

france.text: The first written records for the history of France appeared in the Iron Age. What is now France made up the bulk of the region known to the Romans as Gaul. Greek writers noted the presence of three main ethno-linguistic groups in the area: the Gauls, Aquitani and Belgae.
france.title: History of France

france.text: The culture of France has been shaped by geography, by historical events, and by foreign and internal forces and groups.
france.title: Culture of France

france.text: France has a highly developed social market economy with strong state participation in strategic sectors. It is the world's seventh-largest economy by nominal GDP and the ninth-largest economy by PPP, constituting around 3% of world GDP.
france.title: Economy of France

french-polynesia.text: French Polynesia is located in Oceania. It is a group of six archipelagos in the South Pacific Ocean, about halfway between South America and Australia. Its area is about 4,167 km2, of which 3,827 km2 is land and 340 km2 is water.
french-polynesia.title: Geography of French Polynesia

french-polynesia.text: The economy of French Polynesia is one of a developed country with a service sector accounting for 75%. French Polynesia's GDP per capita is around $22,000, one of the highest in the Pacific region.
french-polynesia.title: Economy of French Polynesia

gabon.text: Gabon is a country in Central Africa, lying along the Atlantic Ocean, just south of the Bight of Biafra.
gabon.title: Geography of Gabon

gabon.text: Present-day Gabon was first inhabited by rainforest hunter-gatherers, attested as early as c. 43,000 BC; archaeology confirms occupations from the Late Pleistocene to the Neolithic along the coast and in the Ogooué.
gabon.title: History of Gabon

gabon.text: The Gabonese people have forged since the independence of the country, in 1960, their own culture which is neither the traditional culture of the different ethnic groups which compose it, nor modern Western culture.
gabon.title: Culture of Gabon

gabon.text: Gabon has a developing economy. It is characterized by strong links with France, large foreign investments, dependence on skilled foreign labor, and decline of agriculture.
gabon.title: Economy of Gabon

georgia.text: Georgia is a country in the Caucasus region on the coast of the Black Sea. Sometimes considered a transcontinental country, it is located at the intersection of Eastern Europe and West Asia, and is today generally regarded as part of Europe.
georgia.title: Geography of Georgia (country)

georgia.text: The nation of Georgia was first unified as a kingdom under the Bagrationi dynasty in 1008 AD, arising from several successor states of the ancient kingdoms of Colchis and Iberia.
georgia.title: History of Georgia (country)

georgia.text: The culture of Georgia has evolved over the country's long history, providing it with a unique national identity and a strong literary tradition based on the Georgian language and alphabet.
georgia.title: Culture of Georgia (country)

georgia.text: The economy of Georgia is an emerging free market economy. Its gross domestic product fell sharply following the dissolution of the Soviet Union but recovered in the mid-2000s, growing in double digits thanks to the economic and democratic reforms brought by the peaceful Rose Revolution.
georgia.title: Economy of Georgia (country)

germany.text: Germany is a country in Central and Western Europe that stretches from the Alps, across the North European Plain to the North Sea and the Baltic Sea. It is the second-most populous country in Europe after Russia, and is seventh-largest country by area in the continent.
germany.title: Geography of Germany

germany.text: The concept of Germany as a distinct region can be traced to Julius Caesar, who referred to the area east of the Rhine as Germania, meaning the land where the Germani live.
germany.title: History of Germany

germany.text: The culture of Germany has been shaped by its central position in Europe and a history spanning over a millennium. Known for significant contributions to art, music, philosophy, religion, science and technology, German culture is diverse and influential.
germany.title: Culture of Germany

germany.text: Germany has a social market economy. As the largest economy in Europe by nominal GDP, Germany's highly developed economy is the third-largest by nominal GDP in the world, as well as the sixth-largest by PPP-adjusted GDP.
germany.title: Economy of Germany

ghana.text: Ghana is a West African country in Africa, along the Gulf of Guinea. Ghana encompasses plains, low hills, rivers, Lake Volta, the world's largest artificial lake, Dodi Island and Bobowasi Island on the south Atlantic Ocean coast of Ghana.
ghana.title: Geography of Ghana

ghana.text: The area of the Republic of Ghana became known in Europe and Arabia as the Ghana Empire after the title of its Emperor, the Ghana.
ghana.title: History of Ghana

ghana.text: Ghana is a country of 33.48 million people and many native groups, such as: The Akans in the center and South of the country, The Ga and Adangbe in, around, and East of Accra, The Guan people in the rainforest, The Dagombas, Mamprusi, and related peoples in the North, The Gurunsi languages speaking peoples in the far North, The Gonjas in the Northern Region.
ghana.title: Culture of Ghana

ghana.text: Ghana has a developing mixed economy. Based on International Monetary Fund estimates, it is the 73rd-largest economy in the world and the 10th-largest economy in Africa by nominal gross domestic product. By purchasing power parity, it ranks 67th globally and 9th in Africa.
ghana.title: Economy of Ghana

gibraltar.text: The history of Gibraltar, a small peninsula on the southern Iberian coast near the entrance of the Mediterranean Sea, spans over 2,900 years. The peninsula was a place of reverence in ancient times, and it later became "one of the most densely fortified and fought-over places in Europe".
gibraltar.title: History of Gibraltar

gibraltar.text: The economy of Gibraltar consists largely of the services sector. While part of the European Union until Brexit, the British overseas territory of Gibraltar has a separate legal jurisdiction from the United Kingdom and a different tax system.
gibraltar.title: Economy of Gibraltar

greece.text: Greece is a country located mostly on the Balkan Peninsula of Southeastern Europe, with thousands of islands stretching to the Anatolian continental shelf of West Asia.
greece.title: Geography of Greece

greece.text: The history of Greece encompasses the history of the territory of the modern nation-state of Greece as well as that of the Greek people and the areas they inhabited and ruled historically.
greece.title: History of Greece

greece.text: The culture of Greece has evolved over thousands of years, beginning in Minoan and later in Mycenaean Greece, continuing most notably into Classical Greece, while influencing the Roman Empire and its successor the Byzantine Empire.
greece.title: Culture of Greece
