united-kingdom.text: The United Kingdom is a country located off the north-western coast of continental Europe. It comprises England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
united-kingdom.title: Geography of the United Kingdom

united-kingdom.text: The history of the United Kingdom begins in 1707 with the Treaty of Union and Acts of Union. The core of the United Kingdom as a unified state came into being with the political union of the kingdoms of England and Scotland, into a new unitary state called Great Britain.
united-kingdom.title: History of the United Kingdom

united-kingdom.text: The culture of the United Kingdom is influenced by the histories of its constituent nations, its interaction with the cultures of Europe, the individual diverse cultures of England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland, and the impact of the British Empire.
united-kingdom.title: Culture of the United Kingdom

united-kingdom.text: The United Kingdom has a highly developed social market economy.
united-kingdom.title: Economy of the United Kingdom

united-states-of-america.text: The term "United States", when used in the geographic sense, refers to the contiguous United States, Alaska, Hawaii, the five insular territories of Puerto Rico, Northern Mariana Islands, U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and minor outlying possessions.
united-states-of-america.title: Geography of the United States

united-states-of-america.text: The history of the United States spans tens of thousands of years of Indigenous civilization; their descendants include but may not be limited to 575 federally recognized tribes.
united-states-of-america.title: History of the United States

united-states-of-america.text: The culture of the United States encompasses various social behaviors, institutions, and norms, including forms of speech, literature, music, visual arts, performing arts, cinema, food, sports, religion, law, technology, as well as other customs, beliefs, and forms of knowledge.
united-states-of-america.title: Culture of the United States

united-states-of-america.text: The United States has a highly developed and diversified market-oriented economy. It is the world's largest economy by nominal GDP, generating 26% of global economic output. It is the second-largest by purchasing power parity.
united-states-of-america.title: Economy of the United States

united-states-virgin-islands.text: The United States Virgin Islands are a group of several dozen islands and cays located in the Caribbean, about 1,100 miles southeast of Florida, 600 miles north of Venezuela, 40 miles east of Puerto Rico, and immediately west and south of the British Virgin Islands. The U.S.
united-states-virgin-islands.title: Geography of the United States Virgin Islands

united-states-virgin-islands.text: The United States Virgin Islands, often abbreviated USVI, are a group of islands and cays located in the Lesser Antilles of the Eastern Caribbean, consisting of three main islands and fifty smaller islets and cays.
united-states-virgin-islands.title: History of the United States Virgin Islands

united-states-virgin-islands.text: The economy of the United States Virgin Islands is primarily dependent upon tourism, trade, and other services, accounting for nearly 60% of the Virgin Island's GDP and about half of total civilian employment. Close to two million tourists per year visit the islands.
united-states-virgin-islands.title: Economy of the United States Virgin Islands

uruguay.text: Uruguay is a country in the southeastern region of South America, bordering the Atlantic Ocean, between Argentina and Brazil. It is located in the Southern Hemisphere on the Atlantic seaboard of South America between 53 and 58 west longitude and 30 and 35 south latitude.
uruguay.title: Geography of Uruguay

uruguay.text: The history of Uruguay comprises different periods: the pre-Columbian time or early history, the Colonial Period, the Period of Nation-Building, and the history of Uruguay as an independent country.
uruguay.title: History of Uruguay

uruguay.text: The culture of Uruguay is diverse since the nation's population is one of multicultural origins.
uruguay.title: Culture of Uruguay

uruguay.text: The economy of Uruguay features an export-oriented agricultural sector and a well-educated workforce, along with high levels of social spending. Tourism and banking are also prominent sectors; Uruguay acts as a regional hub for international finance and tourism.
uruguay.title: Economy of Uruguay

uzbekistan.text: Uzbekistan is a country in Central Asia, located north of Turkmenistan and Afghanistan. With an area of approximately 448,900 square kilometers, Uzbekistan stretches 1,425 km from west to east and 930 km from north to south.
uzbekistan.title: Geography of Uzbekistan

uzbekistan.text: Uzbekistan is a landlocked country in Central Asia. It is itself surrounded by five landlocked countries: Kazakhstan to the north; Kyrgyzstan to the northeast; Tajikistan to the southeast; Afghanistan to the south, Turkmenistan to the south-west. Its capital and largest city is Tashkent.
uzbekistan.title: History of Uzbekistan

uzbekistan.text: The culture of Uzbekistan has a wide mix of ethnic groups and cultures, with the Uzbeks being the majority group. In 1995, approximately 71.5% of Uzbekistan's population was Uzbek. The chief minority groups were Russians, Tajiks, Kazakhs, Tatars, and Karakalpaks.
uzbekistan.title: Culture of Uzbekistan

uzbekistan.text: Uzbekistan has a fast-growing developing economy that is moving away from an old Soviet-style command system towards a modern market economy. It is the second largest economy in Central Asia, after Kazakhstan.
uzbekistan.title: Economy of Uzbekistan

vanuatu.text: Vanuatu, known as the New Hebrides from 1774 until 1980, is a nation and group of around 80 mountainous islands in the South Pacific Ocean. It is part of Oceania. There are several active volcanoes among the islands, the most well-known one being Mount Yasur on Tanna.
vanuatu.title: Geography of Vanuatu

vanuatu.text: The history of Vanuatu spans over 3,000 years. Vanuatu was discovered by Austronesians of the Lapita culture 3,000 years ago. Vanuatu first had contact with Europeans in 1606, when Pedro Fernandes de Queirós, a Portuguese explorer sailing for the Spanish crown, came to the island.
vanuatu.title: History of Vanuatu

vanuatu.text: This article presents an overview of the culture of Vanuatu.
vanuatu.title: Culture of Vanuatu

picture.credit: Phillip Capper from Wellington, New Zealand

vanuatu.text: Vanuatu's economy is primarily agricultural; 80% of the population is engaged in agricultural activities that range from subsistence farming to smallholder farming of coconuts and other cash crops. Copra is by far the most important cash crop, followed by timber, beef, and cocoa.
vanuatu.title: Economy of Vanuatu

vatican-city.text: Vatican City is unique due to the country's position as an urban, landlocked enclave of Rome, Italy. With an area of 49 hectares, and a border with Italy of 3.5 km, it is the world's smallest independent state.
vatican-city.title: Geography of Vatican City

vatican-city.text: Vatican City, officially the Vatican City State, is a landlocked sovereign city-state in Southern Europe. Ruled by the pope, it is an enclave within the city of Rome, Italy, and serves as the administrative centre of the Catholic Church.
vatican-city.title: History of Vatican City

vatican-city.text: The economy of Vatican City is mainly supported financially by the sale of stamps, coins, medals, and tourist mementos as well as fees for admission to museums and publication sales. Vatican City employed 4,822 people in 2016.
vatican-city.title: Economy of Vatican City

venezuela.text: Venezuela is a country in South America, bordering the Caribbean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean, between Colombia and Guyana. It is situated on major sea and air routes linking North and South America.
venezuela.title: Geography of Venezuela

venezuela.text: The history of Venezuela reflects events in areas of the Americas colonized by Spain starting 1502; amid resistance from indigenous peoples, led by Native caciques, such as Guaicaipuro and Tamanaco.
venezuela.title: History of Venezuela

venezuela.text: The culture of Venezuela is a mix of three primary roots: Indigenous, African and Spanish.
venezuela.title: Culture of Venezuela

venezuela.text: Venezuela has a developing economy strongly dependent on its natural resources. Its economic growth is closely linked to petroleum, as the country holds the largest crude oil supply in the world.
venezuela.title: Economy of Venezuela

vietnam.text: Vietnam is located on the eastern margin of the Indochinese peninsula and occupies about 331,211.6 square kilometres, of which about 25% was under cultivation in 1987. It borders China, Laos, and Cambodia and has shorelines along the Gulf of Tonkin, Gulf of Thailand, and Pacific Ocean.
vietnam.title: Geography of Vietnam

vietnam.text: Vietnam, with its coastal strip, rugged mountainous interior, and two major deltas, became home to numerous cultures throughout history.
vietnam.title: History of Vietnam

vietnam.text: The cultures of Vietnam are the customs and traditions of the Viets and the other ethnic groups of Vietnam. Vietnam is part of Southeast Asia and the Sinosphere due to the influence of Chinese culture on Vietnamese culture.
vietnam.title: Culture of Vietnam

vietnam.text: The economy of Vietnam is a developing mixed socialist-oriented market economy. It is the 34th-largest economy in the world by nominal gross domestic product and the 22nd-largest economy in the world by purchasing power parity.
vietnam.title: Economy of Vietnam

wallis-and-futuna.text: Wallis and Futuna, officially the Territory of the Wallis and Futuna Islands, is a French island collectivity in the South Pacific, situated between Tuvalu to the northwest, Fiji to the southwest, Tonga to the southeast, Samoa to the east, and Tokelau to the northeast.
wallis-and-futuna.title: Geography of Wallis and Futuna

wallis-and-futuna.text: This page is an overview of the economy of Wallis and Futuna.
wallis-and-futuna.title: Economy of Wallis and Futuna

western-sahara.text: Western Sahara is a territory in Northern Africa, bordered by the North Atlantic Ocean, Morocco proper, Algeria, and Mauritania. Geographic coordinates: 24°30′N 13°00′W
western-sahara.title: Geography of Western Sahara

western-sahara.text: The people of Western Sahara speak the Ḥassānīya dialect of Arabic, also spoken in northern Mauritania, and Spanish. They are of mixed Arab, African, many consider themselves to be Arab.
western-sahara.title: Culture of Western Sahara

western-sahara.text: The majority of the territory of Western Sahara is currently occupied by the Kingdom of Morocco. As such, the majority of the economic activity of Western Sahara happens in the framework of the economy of Morocco.
western-sahara.title: Economy of Western Sahara

yemen.text: Yemen is located in West Asia, at the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula, between Oman and Saudi Arabia. It is situated at the entrance to the Strait of Bab al-Mandab, which links the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean and is one of the most active and strategic shipping lanes in the world.
yemen.title: Geography of Yemen

yemen.text: Yemen is one of the oldest centers of civilization in the Near East.
yemen.title: History of Yemen

yemen.text: The culture of Yemen has an ancient cultural history. Due to its unique geographic location, Yemen has acquired a very distinctive culture from its neighbors, historically and culturally.
yemen.title: Culture of Yemen

yemen.text: The economy of Yemen is weak and underdeveloped, even more so since the breakout of the Yemeni Civil War which then led to instability and a growing humanitarian crisis. At the time of unification, South Yemen and North Yemen had different but equally struggling underdeveloped economic systems.
yemen.title: Economy of Yemen

zambia.text: Zambia is a landlocked country located in Southern Africa, to the east of Angola. It has a total area of 752,618 square kilometres, of which 9,220 km2 is water.
zambia.title: Geography of Zambia

zambia.text: The history of Zambia experienced many stages from colonisation to independence from Britain on 24 October 1964. Northern Rhodesia became a British sphere of influence in the present-day region of Zambia in 1888, and was officially proclaimed a British protectorate in 1924.
zambia.title: History of Zambia

zambia.text: Zambia, officially the Republic of Zambia, is a landlocked country in Southern Africa.
zambia.title: Culture of Zambia

zambia.text: Zambia has an emerging economy. It is a developing country, and it achieved middle-income status in 2011.
zambia.title: Economy of Zambia

zimbabwe.text: Zimbabwe is a landlocked country in southern Africa lying north of the Tropic of Capricorn. During summer, the whole country experiences warm temperatures as a result of the sun being directly overhead.
zimbabwe.title: Geography of Zimbabwe

zimbabwe.text: Until roughly 2,000 years ago, what would become Zimbabwe was populated by ancestors of the San people. Bantu inhabitants of the region arrived and developed ceramic production in the area. A series of trading empires emerged, including the Kingdom of Mapungubwe and Kingdom of Zimbabwe.
zimbabwe.title: History of Zimbabwe

zimbabwe.text: Zimbabwe has many different cultures, which may include beliefs and ceremonies, one of them being Shona. Zimbabwe's largest ethnic group is Shona.
zimbabwe.title: Culture of Zimbabwe

zimbabwe.text: Zimbabwe has a developing economy. It generates $149.68 billion within its formal economy in PPP terms which translates to 35.9% of the total economy. Agriculture and mining largely contribute to exports. The country has reserves of metallurgical-grade chromite.
zimbabwe.title: Economy of Zimbabwe
